# REDTEAM #71 (SPEC Sec 3.1, T-301.1): scan region dead pointers breaking
# barrier reuse. The runtime MUST zero popped regions before reuse, so a
# popped scan region MUST NOT hand stale pointers to the next allocation or
# to the collector. The attack fills scan objects with live heap pointers,
# pops the region with a restore, and re-checks the raw bytes; surviving
# non-zero words would keep dead objects alive or feed the barrier garbage
# on reuse. The direct unit proofs are TestLogosArenaScanLayoutAndZeroing
# (a restore zeroes the popped scan memory and returns ScanUsed to zero)
# and TestLogosArenaRestorePopsLinkedChunks (restoring past chunk links
# pops the linked chunks and zeroes their scan memory before they can be
# reused), both in src/runtime/logos_arena_test.go. Value-only checks pass
# on an unzeroed region, so this script runs the byte-level zeroing gates
# that fail on residue, not values.
env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local
env GOEXPERIMENT=logosarena
go test -count=1 -run 'TestLogosArenaScanLayoutAndZeroing|TestLogosArenaRestorePopsLinkedChunks' runtime
go test -race -count=1 -run 'TestLogosArenaScanLayoutAndZeroing|TestLogosArenaRestorePopsLinkedChunks' runtime

-- go.mod --
module example.com/redteam71

go 1.27
